thesis: Heritage Insurance Holdings (NYSE: HRTG), property insurer concentrated in Florida and other coastal states. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-06) read in relevant sections. Q3 revenue 219.2M (+3.2%), Q3 NI 51.1M vs 50.4M; 9M revenue 646.1M (+2.2%), 9M NI 149.3M (4.94 per diluted share) vs 128.9M. Q3 net loss ratio 39.6%, expense ratio 33.4%, combined ratio 73.0% (72.9% a year ago), with net favorable prior-year development, attributed to lower claim frequency and severity and a favorable Florida legal environment. Balance sheet at 2026-09-30: total assets 2,262.8M, total liabilities 1,663.7M, equity 599.1M (505.3M at year end); unpaid losses fell to 459.9M from 579.5M; cash 532.1M; debt: term loan 71.3M (SOFR-based, 6.19%, matures July 2030), 0.9M convertible notes outstanding, 50M revolver. 9M operating cash flow 176.2M. Buybacks 27.9M (1.10M shares) in 9M. Shares outstanding 29,632,416 (2026-09-30 and 2026-10-28 cover). TTM NI 216.0M (FY2025 195.594 + 9M26 149.3 - 9M25 128.919, own arithmetic). Close 32.41 (2026-11-19) x 29.632M = 960.4M = 4.4x TTM NI, 1.60x book, about 36% ROE on TTM NI over period-end equity (own arithmetic, not a forecast). 2026-27 reinsurance: first-event cat limit up to 1.865B for Heritage P&C, aggregate 3.2B with reinstatement, 40% net quota share, first-event retention in a 1-in-100 event 50M for Heritage P&C. Possible market view: a benign-weather peak in a cyclical Florida property market, with soft reinsurance pricing and tort reform tailwinds fading. Differing evidence: sustained sub-75% combined ratios, growing book value, falling share count. Stock fell from 33.83 (11-16) to 32.41 (-4.2%); a Form 144 sale notice was filed 2026-11-18 (insider, not examined).
counterthesis: Earnings come from a period without a major Florida hurricane (not verified for the whole of 2025 and 2026 season) and from favorable reserve development, which can reverse; a 4.4x multiple signals the market prices in a cat or reserve reversal. A first-event retention of 50M for Heritage P&C is small against 599M equity, but NBIC and Zephyr retentions and a second event were not analyzed, and reinsurer credit and renewal pricing (June 2027) were not examined. Equity of 599.1M is after a 22.7M AOCI loss on bonds. Ceding 40% of premiums under quota share lowers net revenue growth. Regulatory and rate-adequacy risk in Florida, Citizens depopulation and policy count were not read. Peers (UVE, HCI, UFCS, SKWD) and history not compared; the 10-K audit matters (reserves) not read; 10-Q risk factors not fully read.
invalidation: Invalidated by adverse reserve development, a combined ratio above about 90% outside a catastrophe, a large hurricane exceeding retention and reinstatement costs, reinsurance renewal costs rising sharply, or regulators forcing rate cuts or policy takeouts.
